title: Voltage-drop test: starter and charging circuits
summary: Finds bad cables, grounds and connections that a continuity test misses.
steps: Battery fully charged. Disable fuel or ignition so the engine cranks but doesn't start.
Positive side: one lead on the battery POST (not the clamp), the other on the starter B+ stud. Crank. Reading should be under 0.5 V.
Ground side: one lead on the battery negative POST, the other on the engine block. Crank. Under 0.5 V (0.2 V is better).
Check each connection: across post-to-clamp, should read near 0 V while cranking. Any reading there means a bad connection.
Charging side: engine running at about 2000 rpm with loads on, alternator output stud to battery positive post. Under 0.5 V.
Alternator case to battery negative post, same conditions. Under 0.2 V.
Any high reading: clean, tighten or replace that cable or ground strap, then retest.
